newsitem.title: USA: Procyte study shows Tricomin potential.
newsitem.headline: Procyte study shows Tricomin potential.

text.p: ProCyte Corp said Friday an initial study of its Tricomin solution showed "statistically significant" results that the product could promote hair growth.
Tricomin, a copper peptide compound designated as PC1358, was tried on 36 men ranging in age from 18 to 40 years who have early to mid-stage pattern of hair loss, it said.
The compound was topically applied twice a day for 24 weeks to the participants in the early-stage, Phase II clinical study, it said.

The study's goals were to determine the effect of 1.25 percent and 2.5 percent doses of PC1358 on total hair count and hair weight measured in a one square centimeter treatment area located on the top of the head.

The company said that treatment with the 2.5 percent dosage resulted in a "statistically significant" increase in the total hair count over the course of the study. There were no appreciable increases in total hair weight, it said.

All participants treated with the high dose compound believed they were either growing more hair or staying the same, while almost half of the vehicle-treated participants believed they were losing more hair over the course of the study, it said..
There were no serious drug-related adverse effects that developed in the study, it said.
